description:
Mortgage rates back above 7% as the 10-year Treasury yield tops 5%. What happened, why it happened, and what it means for your mortgage, your job, your grocery bill and your 401(k), explained in plain English with charts built from official data.

CHAPTERS (replace the times after editing)
0:00 The hook
0:00 What happened
0:00 Why it happened
0:00 What it means for you
0:00 What to watch next

SOURCES AND DATA
- 30-year fixed mortgage rate - FRED (Freddie Mac): https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/MORTGAGE30US
- 10-year Treasury yield - FRED (Federal Reserve Board, H.15): https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DGS10
- Median U.S. home sale price - FRED (U.S. Census Bureau and HUD): https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/MSPUS
- 2-year Treasury yield - FRED (Federal Reserve Board, H.15): https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DGS2
- 10-year minus 2-year Treasury yield - FRED (Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis): https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/T10Y2Y
- Unemployment rate - FRED (U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics): https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/UNRATE
- Grocery prices (CPI, food at home) - FRED (U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics): https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/CUSR0000SAF11
- S&P 500 - FRED (S&P Dow Jones Indices): https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/SP500
All charts in this video are drawn from the public data linked above.

NEWS COVERAGE REFERENCED
- Mortgage Rates Ease in Weekly Survey Ahead of JOLTS | Today, November 3, 2026 (The Mortgage Reports): https://themortgagereports.com/mortgage-rates-now/mortgage-rates-today-november-3-2026
- Post-election bond market calm and easing Treasury yields pull borrowing costs to their lowest level in a month (Mortgage Professional America): https://www.mpamag.com/us/mortgage-industry/market-updates/midterm-elections-extend-mortgage-rate-slide-to-three-weeks/596355
- Mortgage rates continue quick retreat (Bankrate via FOX19): https://www.fox19.com/bankrate-article/2026/11/04/mortgage-rates-continue-quick-retreat/

AI DISCLOSURE
Some B-roll in this video is AI-generated and illustrative only. It does not show real people or real events. All charts use real data.

DISCLAIMER
This video is for education and commentary only. It is not investment, tax or legal advice, and nothing in it is a recommendation to buy or sell any security. I am not a licensed financial advisor. Past performance does not guarantee future results. Talk to a licensed professional about your own situation.

clips.caption: Mortgage rates just went back above seven percent.
clips.why: Starts and ends on a complete thought; strong opening line.
clips.opens_with: Mortgage rates just went back above seven percent.
clips.text: Mortgage rates just went back above seven percent. And here's the weird part: the Fed didn't do it. So why is your mortgage getting more expensive? It comes down to one number most people never look at. That number is the ten-year Treasury yield. Think of it as the interest rate the government pays to borrow money for ten years. Banks look at that rate and say, okay, if lending to the government pays this much, a home loan has to pay more. That's the whole trick. So when the ten-year yield goes up, mortgage rates follow it. Not the Fed. The bond market.

clips.caption: Here's what this means for your wallet.
clips.why: Starts and ends on a complete thought; strong opening line.
clips.opens_with: Here's what this means for your wallet.
clips.text: Here's what this means for your wallet. If you already have a fixed-rate mortgage, nothing changes. Your payment is locked. But if you're buying a house right now, the same house costs you hundreds of dollars more every single month than it did a year ago. And that's not because the house got nicer. It's because the price of borrowing money went up. Now why did yields go up in the first place? Three reasons. Oil, inflation, and how much the government is borrowing. When oil gets expensive, almost everything gets more expensive a little later. Gas, shipping, food. That's inflation.

clips.caption: What about your job?
clips.why: Starts and ends on a complete thought; strong opening line.
clips.text: What about your job? Higher borrowing costs make it more expensive for companies to grow, so hiring usually slows down. Your groceries? Those follow oil and shipping costs. Your 401k? Most of it tracks the S and P 500, and stocks do not love higher rates. Here's what to watch next. The Fed meets in December, and the next inflation report comes out before that. This is education, not investment advice. If this helped, subscribe, and tell me what you want explained next.
